findings.title: OAuth application registration documented
findings.detail: Administrators register an OAuth application in OpenProject, set the name and redirect URL, choose scopes, and note the Client ID and secret. Each customer instance needs its own registration in this model.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to developer-owned OAuth on each customer instance

findings.title: api_v3 default scope
findings.detail: If no scope is checked when registering the OAuth application, api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when no other scope is selected on the OAuth application

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: Authorization code flow endpoints
findings.detail: Authorization uses the instance's /oauth/authorize endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, scope and prompt=consent; the code is exchanged at /oauth/token. Access tokens are then sent as bearer tokens.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the user authorization path

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
--url 'https://example.com/oauth/token' \ --header 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <Token>' `

findings.title: Client credentials flow is a separate app actor path
findings.detail: Client credentials flow requests a token with a scope and is distinct from a connected person's user authorization; the optional Client Credentials User acts on behalf of a defined user and is not the customer-connected user model.
findings.appliesWhen: Not the default path for connecting a customer's own account

evidence.quote: --url 'https://example.com/oauth/token' \ --header 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
(Optional) Choose Client Credentials User and define a user on whose behalf requests will be performed.

findings.title: Work package list endpoint with offset pagination
findings.detail: GET /api/v3/work_packages returns a collection with offset and pageSize parameters; the collection exposes total, count and nextByOffset links when offset based pagination is available.

findings.detail: Collections may be paginated; the response includes count, total, pageSize and offset, and further pages are retrieved via the documented links.

findings.title: Subject field is readable
findings.detail: The subject property of a work package is documented as READ / WRITE, so the title is a readable property; read-only use does not require writing it.

steps.title: Read work package titles with pagination on test instance
steps.detail: Scope: read titles of work packages the connected person can access; never modify or delete them. Call GET <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>/api/v3/work_packages?pageSize=100 with header Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN, using the developer-owned OAuth token for the customer's own instance; keep the instance base URL as a user input. Read subject values from the elements array. Pagination is required: follow the nextByOffset link from each response until no nextByOffset link remains, collecting all subjects. Boundary check: perform a safe nonmutating read of the work packages list to confirm the token is accepted; if a denied read is not documented, inspect the actual grant and outgoing request log rather than claiming a narrower token grant. Do not call any write or delete endpoint.
steps.doneWhen: Every page is read via nextByOffset until no nextByOffset link remains, the subject values from all elements arrays are collected, and no write or delete request was sent.

steps.title: Follow nextByOffset to read remaining work package pages
steps.detail: Continue pagination for the same read-only request: for each subsequent page, request the URL from the prior response's nextByOffset link (for example GET <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>/api/v3/work_packages?offset=2&pageSize=100 with Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN), read subjects from its elements array, and repeat until the response contains no nextByOffset link, which is the documented end of the collection. Do not treat two pages as a complete listing. Boundary check: if a page is denied and the denial is not documented, inspect the actual grant and request log rather than assuming a narrower grant. Never send modify or delete requests.
steps.doneWhen: The final page is reached when no nextByOffset link is returned, and all subjects from every page are collected without any modify or delete request.
